% An mwart document: a table of contents, numbered headings at three levels,
% lists, and a bibliography. mwart's \l@section reads \previous@toc@level,
% which the class defines only in \tableofcontents.
\documentclass{mwart}
\title{Mwart}
\author{Someone}
\begin{document}
\maketitle
\tableofcontents
\section{A section}
Some text, as cited in \cite{book} and \cite{paper}.
\subsection{A subsection}
\begin{itemize}
    \item One,
    \begin{itemize}
        \item inside.
    \end{itemize}
    \item two.
\end{itemize}
\subsubsection{A subsubsection}
\begin{enumerate}
    \item First,
    \item second.
\end{enumerate}
\section{Another section}
\begin{description}
    \item[Term] A description.
\end{description}
\begin{thebibliography}{9}
\bibitem{book} A.~Author. \emph{A Book}. 2000.
\bibitem{paper} B.~Writer. A paper. 2001.
\end{thebibliography}
\end{document}
